careful_company_running_windows.guardrai.d: Disabling Defender or adding a scan exclusion removes malware protection.
Turning off the Windows firewall removes host network protection.
Stopping or deleting a security/EDR/event-log service blinds the monitoring stack.
Clearing the Windows event logs destroys the record of what happened on this machine.
Disabling BitLocker decrypts the volume and removes at-rest protection.
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass persistently allows any script to run on this machine.
Disabling PowerShell script-block logging removes the record of what scripts ran.
Bypassing or uninstalling the engine removes the guard that is supervising this session.
Granting an allowlist exception or overriding pack/policy config lets the agent clear its own path.
Editing or deleting the agent's hook configuration can silently remove the engine's protection.
Copying a file ONTO the agent's hook configuration replaces it and can silently remove the engine's protection.
Fetching code and piping it straight into Invoke-Expression runs unreviewed remote code.
powershell -EncodedCommand hides the command being run behind base64.
mshta/regsvr32/rundll32 pointed at a remote payload execute code from the internet.
certutil -urlcache downloads a file from the internet using a certificate utility.

scp with a remote destination copies local files off this machine.
An sftp/WinSCP command with a visible put uploads the named file.
An sftp session to an external host is an interactive transfer channel.
A scripted sftp/ftp/WinSCP session runs transfer commands that are not visible here.
rsync with a remote destination copies local files off this machine.
tftp put uploads a local file to a remote host.
rclone copying to a configured remote sends data to that provider.
rclone rcat/link/serve streams data out, mints a public URL, or exposes a local directory.
aws s3 cp/sync/mv from a local path to s3:// uploads data to S3.
s3api put-object uploads a local file to S3.
aws s3 presign mints a URL that anyone holding it can fetch.
az storage blob upload / azcopy sends local files to Azure Storage.
gsutil/gcloud storage cp from a local path to gs:// uploads data to Cloud Storage.
b2/s3cmd/mc/wrangler r2/supabase upload local files to object storage.
croc/magic-wormhole/ffsend/Taildrop send files directly to another party.
Mounting a WebDAV/HTTP location as a drive creates a file-copy channel over the web.
esentutl /y, diantz, and print /D: copy files to a remote share while posing as other tools.
Publishing a package uploads the project's contents to a registry.
Adding or repointing a git remote changes where a later push sends the repository.

strict_git:push-force-any.d: Force push (even with --force-with-lease) can rewrite remote history. Disabled in strict mode.

strict_git:push-mirror.d: git push --mirror force-updates and deletes remote refs. Disabled in strict mode.

strict_git:push-dynamic-argument.d: Force push risk: a shell-expanded or escaped git push argument cannot be verified as non-forcing. Use literal remote and refspec arguments in strict mode.

strict_git:rebase.d: git rebase rewrites commit history. Disabled in strict mode.

strict_git:commit-amend.d: git commit --amend rewrites the last commit. Disabled in strict mode.

strict_git:cherry-pick.d: git cherry-pick can introduce duplicate commits. Review carefully.

strict_git:filter-branch.d: git filter-branch rewrites entire repository history. Extremely dangerous!

strict_git:filter-repo.d: git filter-repo rewrites repository history. Review carefully.

strict_git:reflog-expire.d: git reflog expire removes reflog entries needed for recovery.

strict_git:gc-aggressive.d: git gc with aggressive/prune options can remove recoverable objects.

strict_git:worktree-remove.d: git worktree remove deletes a linked working tree.

strict_git:submodule-deinit.d: git submodule deinit removes submodule configuration.

strict_git:add-all-dot.d: git add . stages everything including secrets, .env files, and build artifacts. Use 'git add <specific-files>' instead.

strict_git:add-all-flag.d: git add -A/--all stages all changes including secrets, .env files, and build artifacts. Use 'git add <specific-files>' instead.

strict_git:push-master.d: Direct push to master is blocked. Use a feature branch and open a Pull Request.

strict_git:push-main.d: Direct push to main is blocked. Use a feature branch and open a Pull Request.

system.disk:dd-device.d: dd to a block device will OVERWRITE all data on that device. Extremely dangerous!

system.disk:dd-wipe.d: dd from /dev/zero or /dev/urandom to a device will WIPE all data!

system.disk:fdisk-edit.d: fdisk can modify partition tables and cause data loss.

system.disk:parted-modify.d: parted can modify partition tables and cause data loss.

system.disk:mkfs.d: mkfs formats a partition/device and ERASES all existing data.

system.disk:mkswap.d: mkswap formats a partition as a swap area, ERASING any existing data.

system.disk:wipefs.d: wipefs removes filesystem signatures. Use with extreme caution.

system.disk:mount-bind-root.d: mount --bind to root directory can have system-wide effects.

system.disk:umount-force.d: umount -f force unmounts which may cause data loss if device is in use.

system.disk:losetup-device.d: losetup modifies loop device associations. Verify before proceeding.

system.disk:mdadm-stop.d: mdadm --stop shuts down a RAID array. Data may become inaccessible.

system.disk:mdadm-remove.d: mdadm --remove removes a drive from a RAID array. May cause data loss if redundancy is lost.

system.disk:mdadm-fail.d: mdadm --fail marks a device as failed. Use only for intentional drive replacement.

system.disk:mdadm-zero-superblock.d: mdadm --zero-superblock PERMANENTLY erases RAID metadata. Array cannot be reassembled.

system.disk:mdadm-create.d: mdadm --create initializes a new RAID array, ERASING existing data on member devices.

system.disk:mdadm-grow.d: mdadm --grow reshapes a RAID array. Interruption can cause data loss. Backup first.

system.disk:btrfs-subvolume-delete.d: btrfs subvolume delete PERMANENTLY removes a subvolume and all its data.

system.disk:btrfs-device-remove.d: btrfs device remove redistributes data off a device. Interruption causes data loss.

system.disk:btrfs-device-add.d: btrfs device add incorporates a device into the filesystem. Verify the device is correct.

system.disk:btrfs-balance.d: btrfs balance redistributes data across devices. Can be slow and disruptive.

system.disk:btrfs-check-repair.d: btrfs check --repair is DANGEROUS and can cause data loss. Backup first!

system.disk:btrfs-rescue.d: btrfs rescue operations modify filesystem metadata. Use only as last resort.

system.disk:btrfs-filesystem-resize.d: btrfs filesystem resize can shrink a filesystem. Data loss if size is too small.

system.disk:dmsetup-remove.d: dmsetup remove detaches a device-mapper device. May cause data loss if in use.

system.disk:dmsetup-remove-all.d: dmsetup remove_all removes ALL device-mapper devices. Extremely dangerous!

system.disk:dmsetup-wipe-table.d: dmsetup wipe_table replaces the device table, causing all I/O to fail.

system.disk:dmsetup-clear.d: dmsetup clear removes the mapping table from a device.

system.disk:dmsetup-load.d: dmsetup load changes device mapping. Verify the new table is correct.

system.disk:dmsetup-create.d: dmsetup create sets up a new device-mapper device. Verify parameters carefully.

system.disk:nbd-client-disconnect.d: nbd-client -d disconnects a network block device. Data loss if not properly unmounted.

system.disk:nbd-client-connect.d: nbd-client connecting a device can expose or overwrite data. Verify server and device.

system.disk:pvremove.d: pvremove ERASES LVM metadata from a physical volume. Data becomes inaccessible.

system.disk:vgremove.d: vgremove DELETES a volume group and all logical volumes within it.

system.disk:lvremove.d: lvremove PERMANENTLY deletes a logical volume and ALL its data.

system.disk:vgreduce.d: vgreduce removes a physical volume from a volume group. Data may be lost.

system.disk:lvreduce.d: lvreduce SHRINKS a logical volume. Data loss if filesystem isn't resized first!

system.disk:lvresize-shrink.d: lvresize with negative size SHRINKS the volume. Resize filesystem first or lose data!

system.disk:pvmove.d: pvmove migrates data between physical volumes. Do NOT interrupt or data may be lost.

system.disk:lvconvert-merge.d: lvconvert --merge reverts LV to snapshot state, discarding changes since snapshot.

system.disk:diskutil-erase.d: diskutil erase operations DESTROY all data on the target disk or volume.

system.disk:diskutil-partition.d: diskutil partitioning operations rewrite the partition map and erase data.

system.disk:diskutil-apfs-delete.d: diskutil apfs delete/erase operations permanently remove APFS containers, volumes, or snapshots.

system.disk:mkfs-variants.d: This formatter writes a new filesystem over a partition or device and ERASES all existing data.

system.disk:blkdiscard.d: blkdiscard discards every block on a device: the data is gone immediately and cannot be recovered.

system.disk:sgdisk-destroy.d: sgdisk with --zap-all/--clear/--delete/--new rewrites or destroys the partition table.

system.disk:sfdisk-write.d: sfdisk without a read-only flag writes (or deletes) the partition table on a device.

system.disk:gdisk-edit.d: gdisk edits the GPT partition table on a device and can destroy it.

system.disk:nvme-erase.d: nvme format/sanitize/delete-ns erases an NVMe namespace or the whole drive.

system.disk:sg-format.d: sg_format/sg_sanitize low-level formats or sanitizes a SCSI/SAS drive, erasing everything on it.

system.disk:hdparm-erase.d: hdparm security-erase/trim/write-sector destroys data on the drive.

system.disk:cryptsetup-destroy.d: cryptsetup luksFormat/erase destroys the encrypted volume's keys; its data becomes unrecoverable.

system.disk:ddrescue-force.d: ddrescue --force overwrites a block device as its output.

system.disk:badblocks-write.d: badblocks -w runs a destructive write test that overwrites the whole device.

system.disk:zpool-destroy.d: zpool destroy/labelclear destroys a ZFS pool and every dataset in it.

system.disk:zfs-destroy.d: zfs destroy permanently deletes a dataset, volume or snapshot.

system.permissions:chmod-777.d: chmod 777 makes files world-writable. This is a security risk.

system.permissions:chmod-recursive-root.d: chmod -R on system directories can break system permissions.

system.permissions:chown-recursive-root.d: chown -R on system directories can break system ownership.

system.permissions:chmod-setuid.d: Setting setuid bit (chmod u+s) is a security-sensitive operation.

system.permissions:chmod-setgid.d: Setting setgid bit (chmod g+s) is a security-sensitive operation.

system.permissions:chown-to-root.d: Changing ownership to root should be done carefully.

system.permissions:setfacl-all.d: setfacl -R on system directories can modify access control across the filesystem.

system.services:service-stop-critical.d: Stopping critical services can cause system access loss.

system.services:systemctl-isolate.d: systemctl isolate changes the system state significantly.

system.services:systemctl-power.d: systemctl poweroff/reboot/halt will shut down or restart the system.

system.services:shutdown.d: shutdown will power off or restart the system.

system.services:init-level.d: init 0 shuts down, init 6 reboots the system.
